paper_core_claims.claim: An LLM curriculum can propose achievable, progressively harder Minecraft tasks from agent state and exploration history.
Successful LLM-generated JavaScript programs can be described, embedded, stored and retrieved as temporally extended reusable skills that compose through function calls.
Environment feedback, execution errors and GPT-4 self-verification can iteratively refine code and gate skill admission.
Across three author-run trials, Voyager finds about 3.3 times more unique items, travels 2.3 times farther and reaches early tech-tree levels up to 15.3 times faster than adapted baselines.
A learned library transfers to a new world and improves four unseen crafting/collection tasks, while top-five description retrieval is reported at 96.5 percent over 309 samples.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A skill is an async JavaScript function with one bot argument, a generated natural-language description and a task-conditioned success history. Its body composes Mineflayer/control primitives and older skills into a temporally extended policy. The active registry maps the function name to code/description and Chroma indexes the description. This is a concrete executable external function architecture, not a typed, formally specified or sandboxed function calculus.
representation_or_carrier: Minecraft state is rendered as inventory/equipment, nearby blocks/entities, biome/time, health/hunger, position, chests, completed/failed tasks, chat feedback and error events. Skills are JavaScript source plus description text, skills.json and a persistent Chroma vector index. Curriculum QA, progress, chest memory and timestamped event JSON form checkpoint state. Public trial libraries expose final active artifacts but not their event/conversation histories.
specification_language: The enforced callable surface is an async function whose sole parameter is bot; prompts require a meaningful generic name, inventory checks, reuse of provided functions and no loops/recursion. Description prose is at most six sentences. There are no typed inputs/outputs beyond bot, pre/postconditions, declared effects, permissions, dependencies, failure types, version constraints or resource bounds. Task success is a separate critic judgment rather than a contract embedded in the function.
compiler_or_generator: GPT-4 maps task/state/retrieved skills/feedback/errors/critique into JavaScript; Babel parses function declarations and selects the last async one as entry point; the program is executed and refined up to four rounds. GPT-3.5 generates descriptions and embeddings. This is a public execution-guided compiler loop, but it offers no semantic-preservation proof, static effect checking, test generation or guarantee that parser-valid code is safe/correct.
interpreter_or_runtime: Python agents send all active skills/control primitives plus the selected program to a Node/Mineflayer server, which executes the concatenated source through eval against a live bot. Chat/error/observation events return to the next prompt. The runtime is operationally concrete and supports long actions, yet generated code shares the full process and bot authority without sandboxing, time/resource quotas inside eval, capability separation or transaction boundaries.
composition_rule: Top-five description similarity selects prompt-visible skills; GPT-4 composes them and primitives through ordinary JavaScript calls, sequences, branches and awaits. All active programs are also loaded into the execution environment. Names are the registry identity. No type/effect compatibility, dependency graph, name-collision prevention across helpers, behavioral equivalence, regression testing or conflict resolution is defined.
state_or_effect_model: Environment observations and event streams expose mutable inventory, equipment, world blocks/entities, health, hunger, position, chests and time. Code performs mining, crafting, placing, smelting, combat, chest and movement effects. Some failed placement effects can be reversed and crafting tables/furnaces are recycled with commands, but arbitrary JavaScript/world effects have no typed effect signature, permission model, idempotence, compensation or general rollback.
uncertainty_model: Main curves and tables use three trials and report some means plus spread, but no seeds, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests or paired per-world analysis. Temperature zero does not remove hosted-model or world nondeterminism; curriculum uses 0.1 plus unseeded Python prompt-field sampling. Diamond mastery occurs in only one of three Voyager trials. The GPT-4-0613 comparison is visual and described as roughly the same without numeric equivalence criteria. Retrieval accuracy lacks labeling protocol, annotator agreement and class/prevalence details. No calibrated confidence governs curriculum, critic or admission decisions.

validation_regime.formal: algorithm pseudocode and syntax parsing only; no formal semantics, proof, static safety, compiler correctness or non-forgetting theorem
validation_regime.new_skill_admission: a program is admitted when it parses, executes without blocking error and the GPT-4 critic labels the task successful within four attempts; critic mistakes are acknowledged and no independent test/regression suite is created
validation_regime.exploration: three trials per method over up to 160 recorded prompting iterations; appendix releases final item lists but not world seeds, event streams, prompts/responses or exact plotting data
validation_regime.tech_tree: Voyager succeeds 3/3 on wood/stone/iron but only 1/3 on diamond; headline 15.3x uses 6 versus AutoGPT's 92 average wooden-tool iterations
validation_regime.unseen_tasks: Voyager succeeds 3/3 on four tasks; no-skill Voyager also succeeds 3/3 on three tasks and 2/3 on diamond pickaxe but takes more iterations; adapted base ReAct/Reflexion/AutoGPT score 0/3
validation_regime.retrieval: 309 author-labeled samples across the public paper report 80.2 percent top-one and 96.5 percent top-five accuracy, without released queries/relevance labels or annotation method
validation_regime.ablation: six component removals on exploration show large point differences, but raw values, repeated-world pairing and inferential uncertainty are not released
validation_regime.model_variation: v2 adds a GPT-4-0613 curve close to GPT-4-0314, but current public repository predates v2 and no numeric tolerance, logs or exact model-run artifacts are supplied
validation_regime.artifact: public implementation and final three skill libraries are real and syntax-valid; no automated tests, pinned complete dependency lock, trial checkpoints or result-generation scripts are tracked
validation_regime.reproducibility: full paper prompts and core code are public, but deprecated model endpoints, unpinned dependencies, interactive Minecraft/Fabric setup, world seeds, credentials, no result logs and no tests prevent exact current reproduction

equivalence_notions.boundary: Vector similarity is a routing heuristic, not functional equivalence or substitutability.
The same model family supplies an uncalibrated judgment and acknowledged false positives/negatives; no general executable postcondition exists.
Twelve trials over four Minecraft tasks do not establish semantic preservation across arbitrary worlds, agents or domains.
Name identity does not prove behavioral equivalence; historical V2 files are retained without active lineage, comparison or rollback.

lifecycle_and_provenance: Voyager persists completed/failed tasks, QA cache, chest memory, event files, skills.json, descriptions, code and vector databases, enabling resume and cross-world library loading. Function-name collisions write a V2-style historical file while overwriting the active dictionary/vector entry; public libraries therefore have more code files than active skills. It lacks per-skill source task/trace, model/prompt/version, creation timestamp, immutable hash, dependencies, validation receipt, usage/success metrics, semantic version, approval, deprecation, tombstone, migration and active rollback pointer. Git versions the released repository, but the three libraries are final snapshots rather than complete evolution histories.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: The exact source is arXiv v2 under the non-exclusive distribution license; the MIT code head predates v2 and has no immutable paper tag.
Generated JavaScript and the full library execute via Node eval with the bot process's authority; parser checks are not a sandbox or capability boundary.
GPT-4 self-verification is an admission heuristic, not proof of task completion, code correctness or safety; the paper documents verifier failures.
Successful admission creates no regression test, so future composition and environmental changes can silently break a skill.
An existing program name overwrites the active skill/vector record; ever-growing describes accumulated artifacts/capability intent, not a strictly append-only active registry.
Historical V2 code files lack explicit parent links, validation deltas or a restore mechanism.
All active skill code is loaded into the runtime, allowing helper-name collisions and untracked dependencies even though only top-five skills are shown to the generator.
No type/effect system governs inventory/world mutation, external authority, concurrency, idempotence or irreversible actions.
Some environment commands recycle items/blocks and optional failed placements, so measured behavior is a custom instrumented Minecraft setting rather than unrestricted survival play.
README startup requires interactive world selection/open-to-LAN and recommends monitoring; no-human-intervention is bounded to the launched learning loop, not end-to-end operation.
Main evidence uses three trials; no world/random seeds, paired analysis, confidence intervals or significance tests are supplied.
Diamond-tool success is only 1/3, so the only-method-to-unlock claim does not mean reliable mastery.
The 15.3x headline is an early wooden-tool ratio against AutoGPT, not a uniform speedup over all milestones/baselines.
ReAct, Reflexion and AutoGPT are author adaptations to MineDojo/Mineflayer rather than original out-of-box embodied systems; conclusions are conditional on those implementations.
The system uses high-level symbolic state and Mineflayer APIs, not pixels or low-level sensorimotor control, which the authors explicitly exclude.
Final item/terrain lists and libraries are public, but full baseline/Voyager event streams, model conversations, task sequences and plotting inputs are not.
Retrieval relevance labels, annotators and per-query results for 309 samples are absent.
Temperature zero and one later model curve do not establish robustness to API/model/environment variation.
Cost is substantial and endpoint-dependent; the paper gives only a 15x GPT-4/GPT-3.5 ratio, while the repository FAQ gives a historical approximate 50 USD per 160 iterations.
The repository has no automated test suite and broadly unpinned legacy dependencies; static Python compilation is not live reproduction.
Minecraft hallucinations, unachievable curriculum tasks, invalid APIs/fuels, stuck behavior and absent visual perception are acknowledged.
The evidence is Minecraft-specific and does not establish safe robotics deployment, general lifelong learning or immunity to catastrophic forgetting.
The method does not define probabilistic function semantics, calibrated uncertainty, formal equivalence or neural weight composition.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not prove skill correctness, safe execution, semantic composition or non-forgetting.
It does not establish reliable diamond mastery from one success in three trials.
It does not establish deterministic reproduction, statistical significance or broad model/world robustness.
It does not establish an append-only, versioned, provenance-complete or rollback-capable registry.
It does not establish end-to-end autonomous operation without initial human/game setup.
It does not empirically validate ignition, stochastic ignition semantics or weight-space composition.

GAP-017.reason: Similarity retrieval, critic success and cross-world reuse offer operational relatedness signals, not behavioral equivalence or preservation.

GAP-018.reason: Rich world/event effects are observed and fed back, while effect types, permissions, transactions and general rollback are absent.

GAP-019.reason: Persistent checkpoints, code/descriptions, vectors, events and overwrite files support lifecycle, but provenance, versions, admission receipts, deprecation and rollback are incomplete.

GAP-020.reason: Trial variability is reported empirically, but the function/runtime architecture has no probabilistic or stochastic semantics.

N1_FunctionSpec.reason: Named async functions, bot signature, descriptions and task context form a concrete bounded external specification.

N2_Representation.reason: JavaScript, prose, JSON registries, vector embeddings, observations and checkpoints are explicit carriers.

N3_Compiler.reason: Public LLM generation, Babel parsing, execution feedback and iterative repair produce runnable JavaScript.

N4_Artifact.reason: Three public trial libraries contain 51, 52 and 55 active executable skill artifacts plus retained replacement files.

N5_Interpreter.reason: Node/Mineflayer concretely interprets composed skill/control code against a live Minecraft bot.

N6_ExecutionTrace.reason: The recorder persists timestamped event streams and updates item/time/position histories, although paper trial traces are not released.

N7_Validator.reason: Parser, runtime errors, environment feedback and critic gate admission, but no independent postconditions, tests, calibration or regression receipts.

N8_ComposerRouter.reason: Top-five vector retrieval and ordinary JavaScript calls route and compose prior executable skills, bounded by absent compatibility/safety checks.

N9_VersionedRegistry.reason: Persistent active maps, vectors, code snapshots and resume state exist; name overwrite, missing lineage/metadata and no rollback prevent a complete versioned registry.

corrections: Verified the exact v2 paper, all full prompts and the public executable implementation rather than relying on abstract claims.
Confirmed three concrete public learned libraries and distinguished active skills from retained overwritten code files.
Separated parser/runtime/LLM-critic admission from correctness proof, safety validation and regression testing.
Bounded headline ratios to three author-run Minecraft trials and recorded 1/3 diamond mastery.
Separated high-level Mineflayer code control from pixel/sensorimotor embodied learning.
Recorded arbitrary eval execution, untyped effects, interactive setup, missing seeds/traces/tests and incomplete lifecycle governance.
Preserved Function OS support without treating model review or unreproduced trial results as independent empirical validation.

confirmed_projection: Voyager directly and publicly realizes a bounded FunctionSpec-Representation-Compiler-Artifact-Interpreter-ExecutionTrace-Composer architecture: task-conditioned LLM generation produces executable JavaScript skills, feedback repairs them, descriptions/vectors retrieve them, and persistent libraries reuse them across worlds. Confirmation does not extend to formal correctness, sandbox safety, semantic equivalence, robust non-forgetting, general autonomy or complete versioned lifecycle.
source_specific_reasoning: CONFIRMED is warranted for the bounded architecture because the exact paper, complete prompts, public code, runtime and three learned libraries agree on the core function path and expose concrete executable artifacts. The evidence is not upgraded into proof or independent empirical validation: admission depends on an uncalibrated GPT critic; arbitrary JavaScript is eval-executed; active names can overwrite; trial logs/seeds are absent; key claims rest on three runs and diamond mastery is 1/3. These constraints narrow but do not erase the directly implemented Function OS contribution.
projection_boundary: These are 121CX projections from the exact 42-page arXiv v2 PDF, every rendered page, complete source archive, official metadata and the full public MIT repository history through 55e45a8. This model review is not a mechanized proof, live Minecraft/API reproduction, independent trial replication, code-security certification, robotics validation, proof of lifelong non-forgetting, or empirical validation of ignition.
